text: Arkady Godlin As far as I understand, only the very religious Jews consider themselves "chosen." The rest pretty much understand "chosen" as chosen to bear a certain responsibility. What I wish we could figure out - (which by the way nobody has in the whole world) is how to be a Jewish democracy. One where we prioritize the need for a majority Jewish state without that being interpreted as Jewish supremacy or non-Jews having less rights. They should not be mutually exclusive. It's a tough thing to accomplish. And I believe we are up to the task - however we have no chance if the people in charge of the Population Authority and immigration are the very ones that consider themselves actually "chosen" and above everyone else. So I'm just hoping for a change from the top.
